instructions: Hang from a secure bar with arms straight and the body still.

exercises.name: Jack Knife (Suspension)

source_english.description: A suspension jack knife starts in a suspended plank and draws the knees toward the chest as the hips pike upward.
instructions: Place your feet in the suspension straps and set your hands under your shoulders in a high plank.
Brace your trunk and keep the legs straight at the starting position.
Pull your knees toward your chest while lifting the hips into a controlled pike.
Extend the legs back to the plank without letting the hips sag, then repeat.
form_cues: Keep the hands directly under the shoulders.
Move from the hips and abdominals.
Control the straps instead of letting them swing.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hips in the plank.
Using momentum to jerk the knees forward.
Rounding the shoulders or shifting the hands.
source_english.safety_note: Set the straps low enough to keep the feet secure and stop if the suspension becomes unstable.

exercises.name: Kipping Pull Up

source_english.description: Kipping Pull Up pulls from a controlled hang until the chin reaches or clears the bar, then lowers under control.
instructions: Hang from the pull-up bar with an overhand grip and active shoulders.
Alternate smoothly between a hollow body and a slight arch to create a small kip.
As the hips rise, drive the elbows down and pull the chest toward the bar.
Clear the bar with the chin, then extend back to the hanging position under control.
form_cues: Coordinate the hip swing with the pull.
common_mistakes: Dropping from the top without control.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure bar and stop if the shoulder swing becomes painful or uncontrolled.

exercises.name: Knee Raise Parallel Bars

source_english.description: A parallel-bar knee raise supports the body on the bars while both bent knees travel toward the chest.
instructions: Support yourself on the parallel bars with straight arms, shoulders down, and feet off the floor.
Brace your abdomen and bend both knees.
Raise the knees toward the chest without swinging the torso.
Lower the legs slowly until they hang beneath you, then repeat.
form_cues: Use a quiet, controlled bottom position.
common_mistakes: Stopping the descent before control is regained.
source_english.safety_note: Check that the parallel bars are stable and use a smaller range if your grip or shoulders fatigue.

exercises.name: Kneeling Pulldown (band)

source_english.description: A kneeling band pulldown draws the band from an overhead anchor toward the upper chest while the trunk stays tall.
instructions: Anchor the band overhead and kneel facing the anchor with the trunk tall.
Grip the band with both hands and extend the arms overhead.
Pull the elbows down toward the ribs until the hands reach the upper chest.
Pause, then return the arms overhead under steady band tension.
form_cues: Keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
Drive the elbows down, not back.
common_mistakes: Leaning backward to move the band.
Using a band that removes tension at the top.
source_english.safety_note: Secure the anchor and use a band that allows smooth control through the full range.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Band)

source_english.description: Lat Pulldown (Band) pulls the band, cable bar, or machine handles from overhead toward the upper chest while the torso stays braced.
instructions: Attach the band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the band with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms fully overhead, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Engage your lats and pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the ribs stacked and shoulders down.
Drive the elbows toward the torso.
Control the return to the start.
common_mistakes: Leaning or swinging to move the load.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure station and a load or assistance level you can control through the full range.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks

source_english.description: Lateral band walks take controlled side steps against a loop band while the hips remain lowered and the knees track outward.
instructions: Place the loop band above the knees or around the ankles and lower into a shallow athletic stance.
Step sideways with one foot while keeping the band under tension.
Bring the other foot in without letting the knees collapse inward.
Continue for the planned distance, then return in the opposite direction.
form_cues: Stay low with a neutral spine.
Keep tension on the band between steps.
common_mistakes: Allowing the knees to cave inward.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure band and enough space to step without tripping.

source_english.description: Lateral band walks take controlled side steps against a loop band while the hips remain lowered and the knees track outward.
instructions: Place the loop band above the knees or around the ankles and lower into a shallow athletic stance.
Step sideways with one foot while keeping the band under tension.
Bring the other foot in without letting the knees collapse inward.
Continue for the planned distance, then return in the opposite direction.
form_cues: Stay low with a neutral spine.
Keep tension on the band between steps.
common_mistakes: Allowing the knees to cave inward.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure band and enough space to step without tripping.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Band)

source_english.description: Lateral Raise (Band) raises the hands or machine pads out to shoulder height in the frontal plane without swinging.
instructions: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ends at your sides.
Brace the trunk and keep a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise both hands out to the sides until near shoulder height.
Pause, then lower the hands slowly while keeping band tension.
source_english.safety_note: Use light band tension and avoid snapping the band back toward your feet.
